segments: The Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
The affair of Mosul:
Samdaghu went against Jazira,
and built a wall against it,
and began to wage war against it the whole winter and until summer.
Then Khananishoʿ, the Nestorian bishop of that same Jazira,
the one who was prepared on the outside,
and had promised the King of Kings that he knew the art of alchemy,
and as much gold as he wished he would mint {OCR?} for him,
took from the King of Kings a decree of a word of safety (quarter) for the people of Jazira,
and came and entered it.
And the son of ʿIzzaz Bas rose up against him to kill him,
but the leaders did not let him.
And he promised them
that he would go and bring them further confirmation from the King of Kings.
And he went and took a yarligh (decree),
that Jamal al-Din Gulbag,
the slave of Sayf al-Din, the lord of Jazira,
should become king,
and ʿIzz
Bas and Muhammad, the chief of the guard, should be commanders with him,
and Mar the Bishop Khananishoʿ should be adviser and governor and like a father.
And he came and entered Jazira.
And the heart of those who were in it was gladdened,
and they opened the gates.
And Samdaghu entered,
and he gave orders, and in one hour the Tatars demolished the walls of the city;
and they left and went and settled in the valley of Shamamuk {OCR?} in the region of Erbil.
And when the year entered,
1574 [of the Greeks],
Sayf al-Din, the lord of Jazira, sent from Egypt one of his slaves to Jamal al-Din Gulbag, his slave whom he had made king in Jazira,
that he should send him gold that was hidden in such-and-such a place.
And when he took out and gave the gold to that slave,
he took it and went to ʿIzz al-Din Aybeg at ʿImadiyah to tell him the word of his master.
And that one seized him and brought him to Samdaghu.
And he sent and summoned Jamal al-Din Gulbag and accused him,
saying: "We made you king,
and lo, spies are coming to you from Egypt,
and you conceal it from us."
And when he denied it,
he produced the one who had come from Egypt,
and he convicted Gulbag and killed him.
And shortly after, he went to Jazira,
and he also killed those remaining commanders,
and he made Mar the Bishop ruler.
And in the year 1575,
Akki the Erbilite
calumniated Bar Yunis,
the one who had been made king over Mosul,
before the King of Kings,
